title: R3.0F Product Hardening, Migration & Release — schema
note: Defines the legal universe of checkpoints, capabilities, transitions, and authorized-path rules for the R3.0F (final) phase of the R3.0 Integrated Delivery Train. F0 establishes the schema; F1..F6 are NOT yet authorized — they describe future intent so the validator can refuse premature activation. R3.0F depends on R3.0E completing all the way to E5_ACTIVATION before any non-bootstrap F checkpoint may advance — that cross-phase rule is enforced by scripts/check-r3-0-train.js. Per SKYLINE ruling: NO intermediate release; the R3.0 Integrated Delivery Train merges once at F6_RELEASE with package version 2.0.0 and tag v2.0.0 created AFTER merge + new main CI PASS. F6 advancement permits exactly one package.json version bump (1.4.0 → 2.0.0).

releaseStages.note: Monotonic F6_RELEASE progression recorded in checkpoints/F6.json releaseStage. Forward-only: RELEASE_PREPARED (bump staged; no tag/Release) -> RELEASE_TAGGED_DRAFT (annotated tag pushed AND/OR a DRAFT GitHub Release exists; nothing published, no assets) -> RELEASE_PUBLISHED (the GitHub Release is actually published: draft=false with a non-null publishedAt). Semantic ruling (SKYLINE, 2026-07-02): the release_executed capability means PUBLISHED ONLY — a tag alone or a draft Release alone must NOT enable it. Later stages never rewrite earlier evidence; publish advances the stage and fills publishedAt without history rewrites.

authorizedPathRules.note: R3.0F production authorization is by exact repo-relative path only. F6_RELEASE may authorize package.json for a single 1.4.0 → 2.0.0 version bump. No wildcards/regex/globs. The frozen R3.0B persistence schema MUST NOT be modified; F1 migration engine reads/writes via migration scripts only.
